properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to OLYMPUS ENERGY, LLC in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/30/2025 to OLYMPUS ENERGY, LLC in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OLYMPUS ENERGY, LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8240283
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: On June 30, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of Olympus Energy's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/27/2025 at 2:37 pm.The spill report stated that at 1:15 pm on 6/27/2025, over 5 gallons of a produced water (Photo 12), fresh water, and frack chemicals (Photos 13-15) mixture was released on containment and on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site.Accompanying during today's inspection is Olympus representative Laura Karosic.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had all required components.At the time of this inspection, zipper frack operations were being conducted on 2 Utica wells with 57 out of 153 fracks remaining.At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that a hose connected to the blender ruptured spraying the mixture on and off containment, however no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to a fresh water impoundment located on site. The graveled well pad in this incident appeared to be scraped, the ground in this area was observed to be brown and muddy in comparison to the dry and gray graveled well pad surrounding this area. Ms. Karosic stated that 2-4 inches of the well pad in this incident area was scraped and vacuums were used to suck up any puddles of fluid. The secondary containment where this incident occurred appeared to be clean and dry.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed 3 clamshell dumpsters on site, 2 were full of contaminated material and the 3rd will be filled with any remaining contaminated material once Moody arrives to conduct further remediation efforts.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected readings of 8.30 mS, 3.07 mS and 2.20 mS in the incident area and 8.21 mS underneath/at the base of the clean water impoundment. The area outside of this incident area where the ground was not scraped was also screened and the readings collected in that area was comparable to the background reading of 0.333 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign. At the time of this inspection, the DEP notified Ms. Karosic of the elevated soil conductivity readings in the incident area and underneath the fresh water impoundment. Ms. Karosic stated that fracking operations is scheduled to commence between July 10-11, 2025, then the fresh water impoundment will be removed and remediation can be conducted in the area where the impoundment was located. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that at this time they estimate that the quantity of the release is between 1 and 3 barrels and that they anticipate following Act 2 protocol for the clean up. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed SDSs for all chemicals on site and included in the release mixture to be located in the on site trailer. Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the 1-3 barrel release of produced water, fresh water, and fracking chemicals on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/01/2024 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/01/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8177801
Permit API: 081-21938
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/01/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of 10 barrels of produced water. It was reported that there were 2 barrels off of containment and 8 barrels on containment. The release occurred from a low pressure line on a fracking pump while the line was being flushed with fresh water from an AST onsite. The mixture of fresh and produced water sprayed out as a mist over the secondary containment and the pad. The release was reported around 23:00 on 2/29/24.The affected area was about 60' southeast of the wells near the center of the pad. Tobias Welding and Machining began scraping the impacted area on 2/29/24. On 3/1/24, Penn E and R arrived and continued to scrape the area based on visual and conductivity screening. The scraped area was about 77' by 26' around and 2" to 4" deep. Penn E and R was in the process of setting up confirmation sampling for Act 2 remediation.DEP screened for conductivity inside and surrounding the scraped area. Puddles within the scraped area ranged from 0.84 to 0.96 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and the soil was below 0.10 mS/cm. Puddles surrounding the scraped area were 0.34 to 0.65 mS/cm. Soil conductivity readings were attempted outside the impacted area but the pad was too compacted.The removed material was being hauled to the neighboring Bieber Sisters Pad A where it was stored in a covered rolloff container on secondary containment. The material will remain on the pad until characterization samples are completed and it can be properly disposed of. Photo 3 shows the rolloff with about half of the removed material. The rest of the material was being hauled to the rolloff while DEP was leaving the site.Based on a conversation with Zac Subra, EQT, the initial reported volume of the release may have been overestimated. However, since an exact volume was not know EQT will still follow the remediation requirements of Act 2.It is recommended that the pad be screened when secondary containment is pulled to be certain that no produced water seeped under the containment as a result of the release.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), 78a56(a), and SWMA 301.

Comments: On January 7, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline and Chris Southard conducted a routine site inspection at the Frontier Natural Resources Winner 1 project. There is 1 well at the site and was set to regulatory inactive status on August 27, 2013. The regulatory inactive status expired on August 27, 2014 and at this time is considered abandoned. The DEP recommends sending a notification that the well is to go on regulatory inactive status, change to active status or choose to plug the well. The weekly E&S inspection log was found onsite for review. According to the last entry on the E&S log, the site was last inspected on August 29, 2019. Even though the ESCGP is expired the operator is still required to conduct weekly inspections or after a storm water event in accordance with Chapter 102.4(a) or until the permit is terminated by the Department. The ESCGP expired on 12/22/2016. Since the ESCGP permit is expired, no earth disturbance activities can occur until the operator obtains a new ESCGP from the Department. The Department recommends applying for a new ESCGP and restoring the site. Multiple violations are still outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/15/2025 to TITUS ENERGY LLC in Monroe Township, Clarion county. 78.73(f) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to equip well with a check valve to prevent backflow from the pipelines into the well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TITUS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2025
Violation Code: 78.73(f) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to equip well with a check valve to prevent backflow from the pipelines into the well.
Violation ID: 8233564
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing investigation into stray gas migration, involving combustible gas detected at the foundation of a nearby private residence. The well is situated approximately 650 feet north-northwest of the complainant’s residence. During the inspection, an updated well record was reviewed. The well was actively producing via the 4-inch production string, with valves on the 7-inch intermediate casing and the 4-inch production string annuls closed at the time of inspection Bubbling was observed in the annular space between the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing. Combustible gas screening using a calibrated gas meter indicated a concentration of 29% LEL (1.4%) in this annulus. According to the well records, both the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing were cemented to surface. The presence of combustible gas in the annulus suggests potential defects in the casing and/or cement integrity. Additionally, no check valve was observed on the production lines exiting the well. To further assess possible migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the wellhead in the cardinal directions, each about 3 feet deep. No detectable levels of combustible gas were found in the slam bar holes at the time of the inspection. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on 05/15/2025 was used for combustible gas screening during the inspection. It is noted that the operator has not responded to or completed the recommended corrective actions outlined in Inspection ID# 3913271. These actions were communicated via certified mail (USPS# 9589 0710 5270 1975 0616 42), sent on 02/13/2025 and received by the operator on 02/19/2025. As a result, the violations identified during this inspection are now being formally imposed on this well.

Violation ID 777003
Permit API 005-28726
Unconventional N
County Armstrong
Municipality Redbank Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2017-01-18
Comments Inspection performed in response to Operator’s reported release of 29bbl (1218gal). production water to the ground on 1/17/2017. According to the Operator, the spill occurred due to a crack at the base of the tank caused by an animal burrowing beneath the tank. Operator estimated the release volume based on weekly tank readings that were previously obtained. At the time of inspection, Operator on site, clean-up work ongoing. During inspection, Department confirmed Operator's reported cause of spill as indicated by a visible hairline crack at the base of the brine tank. Compromised brine tank disconnected from production equipment and moved to enable access to impacted area. Impacted area measuring approximately 8’x8’ being excavated and material placed in two roll off containers for proper disposal. Excavation of impacted area will be performed until all impacted material is recovered as indicated by conductivity measurements. Site appears to be stable with no E&S issues. Department recommends Operator perform clean-up in accordance with policy and forward copies of all sampling test results, tank readings and reports upon receipt. Department requests Operator provide a written response detailing the cause, nature and type of materials released, the affected media, any surrounding impacts to water supplies and/or buildings, remediation method selected and actions taken to remediate and future actions/plans to prevent such incidents. Violations are being issued under 25 PA CODE 78a. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending Departmental investigation. Department will conduct a follow-up inspection.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to Pennfield Energy's 8/17/2021 notification of a crude oil discharge from a stock tank located at the Milford South tank battery, which is located adjacent to this well site. Per Matt Duckett (field representative for Pennfield Energy) the oil/water separator that serves this tank battery failed and resulted in all production fluids entering the stock tank, which did not have the capacity to hold all of the fluid. Crude oil then discharged from an open vent on top of one of the stock tanks and onto the ground within an earthen containment that surrounds all of the tanks at the Milford South tank battery. The estimated quantity of crude oil that was released has been revised after conducting remediation work. Matt Duckett stated that approximately five barrels of crude is a more accurate quantity of product actually released as a result of this incident. Additional details regarding the release can be found in the 'Remarks/Violations' section of this report. This well is equipped for production with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack's electric box.

Unconventional: No
County: McKean

Inspection Date: 1/03/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well. This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. There are no apparent surface issues on the location location or the spur road leading to it.A tank battery located along FR 370 approximately 250 feet northwest of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks (11883 and 11884) within an earthen containment. There is evidence of repeated discharges of production water inside of the containment from each tank. Soil specific conductance (SPC) readings upwards of 15,000 uS/cm were detected at/downslope of the drains located on the back side of each tank. Elevated SPC is prevalent across the ground inside of the containment downslope of the tanks. Accumulated fluid pooled along the western wall of the containment has an SPC over 20,000 uS/cm. There was no active discharge at time of inspection.The fluids released inside of the containment have seeped through the northern corner of the earthen containment wall (or there is a buried drain) at 41.99216N / 78.76119 W. There is an approximate 25' x 3' area of stained soil with elevated SPC (upwards of 818 uS/cm vs 40 uS/cm of nearby uncontaminated soil) present outside of the containment's northern corner. The end of the apparent contaminated soil is located approximately 75 feet from Yeager Brook.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery containment to contain fluid inside of it will also nee to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Comments: On April 17, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View LTV 2 well located in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3715546 where violations were issued for a release and for IR 3882155 where violations were continued due to site conditions being unchanged. The LTV 2 site is located within abandoned coal mine land and therefore the well site is composed of coal refuge. Mountain View Operator Dave Lindahl informed the Department via email (documented in IR 3797419) that this abandoned coal mine land is to be remediated by the Department's Clean Streams Program and that this well site is included in their remediationplans. Comments: Due to COVID-19 restrictions, an admin inspection is being conducted. This inspection is being conducted in response to a report submitted by the operator on May 16, 2020 at approximately 9:55 PM via the DEP hotline that a spill of approximately 10 gallons of Production Fluid occurred on the Prentice Well Pad located in Forward Township, Allegheny County. The Department contacted the operator via telephone at approximately 8:45 AM on May 18, 2020 to follow up. Based on this conversation, the operator stated that they believed a water truck was responsible for the leak, which went from the Production Tanks, across the pad, down the access road, and onto a public roadway. The operator stated that no WOTC were impacted or potentially impacted by this spill. The operator stated they had dispatched SPSI for remediation immediately, and that visibly impacted material was removed using a skid loader, the public road was cleaned up using gator-sorb. The Operator stated that remediation was completed by Sunday afternoon (May 17, 2020). The Operator mentioned that recorded video of the event from security cameras had probably caught the incident occurring. The Department is requesting any and all evidence that may have documented this incident. The Department is requesting additional information on the water truck including but not limited to, records of production fluid on the truck prior to accessing the site, how much was removed from the Production Tanks at Prentice, and the total that was off loaded after leaving the Prentice site to be submitted to the Department by 5/29/2020. The Department is also requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted as soon as possible. Photos attached to this inspection were provided by the operator. Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, and further investigation, more violations may be issued.

Comments: On 11/21/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alterations inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 36 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Rainfall had impacted the region in the past 24 hours.Inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I did witness a secondary containment structure containing drilling mats with water at the level of the containment wall and fluid from the containment on the unprotected ground (picture 5). The water field tested at 0.301 mS conductance. Seneca's Jeff Passerrello was notified and was scheduling to have the containment emptied.Anthony Murphy described current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet has finished completion operations on five new wells at the site. Two snubbing/well servicing units were on site, drilling plugs out of the five completed wells. The units were on the first two wells and Anthony expects it to take a week to drill plugs on each well. He expects the crews to finish drilling plugs on all five wells by 12/10/2024. Anthony accompanied me on the site inspection. All operations were being conducted within a plastic lined containment structure that was protected by drilling mats. I did witness frac tanks, gas buster tanks, vac boxes and various chemical totes staged in secondary containment. There were ten frac tanks with fresh and produced water, six gas busters, and eight vac boxes staged near the snubbing/servicing units all staged in secondary containment. 28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness water in the transfer manifold duck pond on the west side of the snubbing units that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. Anthony will have the liquids removed.During the inspection, I did witness a 5' x 8' water puddle near the north-central pad outfall that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-145. The upper conductivity limit of the Oakton PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. Water discharging from the north-central pad outfall into the sediment basin field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-146 and soil sample 9551-147. Water in the basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 3.07 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-148. Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. As recommended in the inspections listed above, the DEP continues to recommend pursuing Act 2 for the large amount of elevated conductance fluids discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin.The DEP recommends the following: 1. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.3. Monitor secondary containment structures for contaminants, for liquid levels and for adequate freeboard levels; remove liquids as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

The spill occurred on the ROW of the DTE Susquehanna Gathering Well Connect 67 Pipeline at a waterline valve cellar located at latitude 41.876168 and longitude -75.583155 also located in Jackson Township. The waterline was installed by DTE but is owned and operated by SWN. On 4/25/19, DTE operations personnel were conducting an annual inspection of their Well Connect 67 Pipeline and identified a three quarter inch line with a leaking quarter turn ball relief valve located above the lid of the waterline valve cellar, as shown in Photo #1. Photo #2 shows the extent of the accelerated corrosion caused by the leak to the lid. The DTE Operations personnel then contacted their Operations management team who then contacted SWN's Production group at 1:30 PM, that same day, 4/25/19. On 4/26/19 at 1:40 PM, SWN confirmed that the water within the cellar did show elevated conductivity. On 4/26/19 at 3:01 PM, Mike Deming, SWN Senior Regulatory Analyst left a voice message on my cell phone. Mr. Deming then attempted to contact Briana Cunningham at 3:01 PM and left a voice message. At 3:05 PM, Briana Cunningham contacted Mike Deming by phone who then explained the conditions listed above and noted that their conductivity readings showed the conductivity of the water within the valve cellar to be above the meter's capability of 19.9 milli Siemens. SWN measured the soil conductivity just off the valve cellar lid where the leak was running off the lid to be at 6.27 milli Siemens. Among those personnel also present during the inspection today were Brianna Cunningham, Dept. WQSS, Eric Rooney, Dept. P.G., Jon Sassi, Dept. EPS, Cassidy Moyer, Dept. WQST, Mike Spangenberg, DTE Senior Environmental Manager, Mike Deming, SWN Senior Regulatory Analyst, Seth Tratthen, Senior Regulatory Analyst, Dawn Washo, Resource Environmental P.G., Project Manager, Abbey Vogler Resource Environmental G.I.T., Environmental Specialist, and Christian Mondi, Resource Environmental Data Specialist. Mike Deming stated that on 4/26/19 during the evening, 200 gallons of water was removed from the valve cellar. As Photo #1 shows, the valve cellar is made from a large corrugated pipe, and is designed to maintain the valve pit, but does not function as containment, as there is no bottom in this cellar. During the inspection, water was observed in the valve cellar, which is approximately 8' deep. Mike Deming stated that the water level in the cellar was at about the same height as it was on 4/25/19 when they removed and emptied the cellar, which would suggest that there is at least 200 gallons of water currently present in the cellar. Samples were collected from the valve cellar, a seep downgradient of the valve cellar, and samples collected from upstream and downstream of an ephemeral steam which the seep directly discharges to. Mike Spangenberg stated that prior to this leak discovery, DTE last inspected this line in June of 2018. Mike Deming states that this line was last utilized by SWN to stimulate their Gremmel 2H between March 2nd and March 31st of this year, 2019. A phone discussion with Steve Moyer revealed that when the leak was found on 4/25/19, it was leaking, which means that the blended fluid/water dripping from the damaged relief valve was due to back pressure of blended fluid/water laying in the line, even though the water line valve at this location was open. The water utilized during the 2H stimulation came from SWNs Young and Zeffer Impoundments.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/27/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 940413
Permit API: 015-22501
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Monroe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/28/2021
Comments: Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) notified Carrie Knapp (NCRO) that at 1530 hrs Monday December 27, 2021 they discovered approximately 112 barrels of produced water/freshwater spilled. A flowback tank in containment leaked, and the containment leaked onto the pad. (CTS 361265). I spoke with William Dolan (Creston Environmental LLC) on site. He explained they are using a YSI meter and a soil probe to delineate the extent of the reported 112 barrel brine/freshwater mix release to the pad surface which occurred yesterday. A vac truck with a T adapter (photo) is removing that liquid from the pad surface. A track hoe (photo) is removing the impacted pad soil/rock and loading into a dump-truck. The truck then dumps the material on liner containment (photo) on the opposite side of the pad. I used an Oakton PCSTestr 35 to get electrical conductivity (EC) readings from pooled liquid on the pad surface. In the area where the release occurred, it gave readings of 8.0-12.2 mS/cm. I collected liquid sample 0935-429 from the area that was 12.2 mS/cm. Pooled liquid on the pad surface unaffected by the release is 0.16-0.22 mS/cm. I also used a Hanna soil probe to get EC readings from the pad material. In the excavated area it gave a 0.04 mS/cm reading; the unexcavated area immediately outside it gave readings of 3.0-4.0 mS/cm. 4.0 mS /cm is the max limit for the Hanna soil probe. The EC readings indicate the brine release did not flow outside of the pad surface. Rock, vegetation, and straw mulch stabilize soil of the site. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Cleanup of this spill will be referred to the DEP ECB program for Act 2 compliance. Air temp 40F JLP

Comments: On site today to witness the beginning of the Koromlan 1H, 4H, 6H and 107HC (72 hr.) Pressure Build Up Tests (PBUTs). Upon arrival all (4) wells were in automated production with all annuli open and venting. Creston Consultants reps. (Jason Rajon and Ryan Carmody) were on site to perform pressure checks with a Cristal digital pressure gauge and gas screenings with a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer. The results of the gas screenings and flow checks for each well are listed below: - If the flow test showed flow under 0.02 SLPM, a balloon was placed over open vent pipe for 10 minutes to check for any inflation of ballon indicating small amount of flow. - 1H - (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no balloon inflation); 25% gas initially, 5% gas peak and 5% gas sustained (9x5) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no balloon inflation); 45% gas initially, 10% peak and 10% gas sustained. - 4H - (20x13) annulus: 8.8 Cu/ft per day; 28% gas initially, 10% gas peak and 10% gas sustained. (13x9) annulus: 1.1 Cu/ft per day; 14% gas initially, 6% gas peak and 5% gas sustained (30sec.). (9x5) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no balloon inflation; 26% gas initially, 21,020 ppm peak and 20,000 ppm gas sustained (30 sec.) - 6H - (13x9) annulus: 4.8 Cu/ft per day; 18% gas initially, 13% gas peak and 13% gas sustained. (9x5) annulus: 1.9 Cu/ft per day; 29% gas initially, 11% peak and 10% gas sustained - 107HC - (20x13) annulus: under Cu/ft per day(no ballon inflation); 20 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained. (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no ballon inflation); 160 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained. (9x5) annulus: 1.7 Cu/ft per day; 55% gas initially, 16,080 ppm gas peak and 14,000 ppm gas sustained (30sec.). - All annuli were shut in at 12:30pm (3/24/25) with the exception of the 4H (20x13) annulus which will be shut in on Wed. (3/26/25) resulting in a 24hr. test for this annulus.
